chosen_property.label: about
chosen_property.justification: The 'about' property directly links an Event to a Thing (Person/PerformingGroup) as its subject matter.

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.

candidates.label: mainEntityOfPage
candidates.comment: A main entity of page relation between a thing and the creative work or URL for which it is the primary described entity. Also called: primary page, described on page, featured on page. Examples: "Albert Einstein mainEntityOfPage Wikipedia Article", "The Election mainEntityOfPage News Report", "Quantum Physics mainEntityOfPage Research Paper". Distinct from mainEntity, which indicates the primary entity described in a creative work.

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: mainContentOfPage
candidates.comment: A main content relation between a web page and the web page element that constitutes its primary subject. Also called: primary content, central element, core content. Examples: "Article Page mainContentOfPage ArticleBody", "Product Page mainContentOfPage ProductDescription", "Blog Post mainContentOfPage PostContent".

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

relations.definition: Specifies the age of a person at the time of an event.
relations.embedding_query_text: at age: Specifies the age of a person at the time of an event.

chosen_property.label: ageAtEvent
chosen_property.definition: The age of a person at the time a specific event occurred.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property links an Event to a Duration representing the age of a person at that event.

candidates.label: requiredMinAge
candidates.comment: A required minimum age relation between a people audience and the lower age limit for inclusion. Also called min age, age requirement. Examples: "An adult event targets a people audience with required min age '18'.", "A driving course has a required min age '16'.", "A senior discount applies to a people audience with required min age '65'."

candidates.label: requiredMaxAge
candidates.comment: A required maximum age relation between a people audience and the upper age limit for inclusion. Also called max age, age limit. Examples: "A children's event targets a people audience with required max age '12'.", "A youth program has a required max age '25'.", "A senior discount applies to a people audience with required max age '99'."

candidates.label: typicalAgeRange
candidates.comment: A typical age range relation between a creative work or event and the expected age group of its audience. Also called age suitability, target age, recommended age. Examples: "Book typicalAgeRange '7-9'", "Movie typicalAgeRange '13+'", "Event typicalAgeRange 'all ages'".

candidates.label: suggestedAge
candidates.comment: A quantitative value indicating the recommended age or age range for an intended audience or person. Also called "recommended age", "age range", "target age", "suitable age". Examples: "The toy has suggestedAge 3-5 years", "The audience specification includes suggestedAge 18+", "This product is for suggestedAge 6-12 months.". Distinct from suggestedMinAge and suggestedMaxAge, which specify only the minimum or maximum.

candidates.label: suggestedMinAge
candidates.comment: A numerical value indicating the minimum recommended age in years for an audience or user. Also called "minimum age", "lower age limit", "age floor". Examples: "The game has suggestedMinAge 7", "The audience specification includes suggestedMinAge 18", "This content is suitable from suggestedMinAge 3.". Distinct from suggestedAge, which specifies a range, and suggestedMaxAge, which specifies only the maximum.

candidates.label: suggestedMaxAge
candidates.comment: A numerical value indicating the maximum recommended age in years for an audience or user. Also called "maximum age", "upper age limit", "age cap". Examples: "The game has suggestedMaxAge 12", "The audience specification includes suggestedMaxAge 65", "This content is suitable up to suggestedMaxAge 18.". Distinct from suggestedAge, which specifies a range, and suggestedMinAge, which specifies only the minimum.

candidates.label: childMinAge
candidates.comment: A demographic specification for a parent audience, indicating the minimal age of a child. Also called "minimum child age", "lower age limit for child", "child age floor". Examples: "Parent audience for infants childMinAge 0", "Parent audience for school-age children childMinAge 5". Distinct from childMaxAge, which specifies the maximal age.

candidates.label: childMaxAge
candidates.comment: A demographic specification for a parent audience, indicating the maximal age of a child. Also called "maximum child age", "upper age limit for child", "child age cap". Examples: "Parent audience for toddlers childMaxAge 3", "Parent audience for teens childMaxAge 17". Distinct from childMinAge, which specifies the minimal age.

candidates.label: yearsInOperation
candidates.comment: An operational age relation between a business audience and a quantitative value, indicating the number of years the business has been active. Also called business age, operational duration, years active. Examples: TargetAudience yearsInOperation "5-10 years", BusinessAudience yearsInOperation "over 20 years", StartupAudience yearsInOperation "under 2 years".

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim

Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: sourcedFrom
candidates.comment: An anatomical origin relation between a nerve and the brain structure from which its neurons originate. Also called "originates from", "nerve pathway source", "derived from brain structure". Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: provider
candidates.comment: A provision relation between an action, work, program, or service and the organization or person that supplies or performs it. Also called supplied by, performed by, offered by, produced by. Examples: "A parcel delivery is provided by FedEx.", "A financial incentive is provided by the government.", "A medical service is provided by Dr. Smith."

candidates.label: unnamedSourcesPolicy
candidates.comment: An unnamed sources policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a statement about its policy on using unnamed sources. Also called anonymous sources policy, source confidentiality policy, disclosure policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/sources-policy'", "Organization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'Our policy requires two independent sources.'", "News outlet unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/ethics'".

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

chosen_property.label: announcesEvent
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the event that is made public by an announcement.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly links an Announcement to the Event being announced.

candidates.label: announcementLocation
candidates.comment: An announcement location relation between a special announcement and the specific civic structure or local business it pertains to. Also called relevant location, associated place, specific venue. Examples: "A special announcement's announcement location is 'City Hall'.", "The emergency announcement's announcement location is 'Local Grocery Store'." Distinct from spatialCoverage, which is used for larger geographic regions.

candidates.label: releasedEvent
candidates.comment: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."

candidates.label: publicTransportClosuresInfo
candidates.comment: A public transport closures information relation between a special announcement and details regarding public transport disruptions. Also called transport closure details, public transit alerts. Examples: "A special announcement includes public transport closures info about subway lines.", "An emergency alert provides public transport closures info for bus routes.", "A news update contains public transport closures info for train services."

candidates.label: quarantineGuidelines
candidates.comment: A quarantine guidelines relation between a special announcement and information regarding quarantine rules. Also called isolation rules, self-quarantine instructions. Examples: "A special announcement provides quarantine guidelines for travelers.", "A public health update includes quarantine guidelines for close contacts.", "A government notice details quarantine guidelines for returning citizens."

candidates.label: diseasePreventionInfo
candidates.comment: A disease prevention information relation between a special announcement and a URL or web content providing details about disease prevention. Also called "prevention guidelines", "health advice". Examples: "Special announcement diseasePreventionInfo 'cdc.gov/prevention'", "Public health alert diseasePreventionInfo 'WebContent on handwashing'", "COVID-19 update diseasePreventionInfo 'who.int/prevention'".

candidates.label: diseaseSpreadStatistics
candidates.comment: A disease spread statistics relation between a special announcement and a dataset, observation, URL, or web content containing statistical information about the spread of a disease. Also called "epidemic data", "infection rates", "case statistics". Examples: "Special announcement diseaseSpreadStatistics 'Dataset of daily cases'", "Public health update diseaseSpreadStatistics 'WebContent on regional spread'", "COVID-19 alert diseaseSpreadStatistics 'URL to dashboard'".

candidates.label: gettingTestedInfo
candidates.comment: A getting tested info relation between a special announcement and information regarding testing for a medical condition. Also called: testing information, diagnostic details, screening guidance. Examples: "COVID-19 Announcement" getting tested info "CDC Testing Guidelines", "Flu Season Alert" getting tested info "Local Clinic Testing Sites", "Public Health Notice" getting tested info "Symptoms and Testing Advice".

candidates.label: newsUpdatesAndGuidelines
candidates.comment: A URL or web content providing news updates and guidelines related to a special announcement. Also called updates page, guidelines link, news and guidance. Examples: "COVID-19 Announcement newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://example.com/covid-updates'", "Emergency Alert newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://gov.example.org/emergency-guidelines'", "Product Recall newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://company.com/recall-info'".

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: governmentBenefitsInfo
candidates.comment: A government benefits info relation between a special announcement and information about associated government services or benefits. Also called: public aid details, government assistance, benefit programs. Examples: "Pandemic Relief Announcement" government benefits info "Unemployment Benefits Program", "Housing Crisis Alert" government benefits info "Rental Assistance Program", "Disaster Recovery Notice" government benefits info "FEMA Aid Services".

relations.definition: Indicates the representative or manager of a person.
relations.embedding_query_text: has agent: Indicates the representative or manager of a person.

chosen_property.label: hasAgent
chosen_property.definition: Indicates a person's representative or agent.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly links a Person to another Person as their agent or representative.

candidates.label: agentInteractionStatistic
candidates.comment: An agent interaction statistic relation between an organization or person and a counter representing their completed interactions in a specific agent role and context. Also called interaction count, activity metric, engagement statistic. Examples: "A customer service agent's interaction statistic shows '150 calls handled'.", "A company's agent interaction statistic indicates '1000 sales completed'."

candidates.label: agent
candidates.comment: An agent relation between an action and the organization or person who directly performs or drives it. Also called performer, doer, initiator, actor. Examples: "A 'write book' action's agent is 'John Doe'.", "A 'deliver package' action's agent is 'Delivery Service Inc'."

candidates.label: broker
candidates.comment: An intermediary relation between an invoice, order, reservation, or service and the organization or person who arranges the exchange. Also called "arranged by", "intermediary", "agent". Examples: "Flight reservation broker Expedia", "Real estate service broker John Doe", "Stock order broker Fidelity". Distinct from seller or buyer, which indicate direct parties in an exchange, whereas broker facilitates it without taking ownership.

candidates.label: bookingAgent
candidates.comment: An organization or person acting as a broker or booking agent for a reservation. Also called: reservation agent, travel agent, broker. Examples: "Reservation 'Hotel Stay' bookingAgent 'Booking.com'", "Reservation 'Flight' bookingAgent 'Travel Agency X'."

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: hasOfferCatalog
candidates.comment: An offer catalog relation between an organization, person, or service and an associated offer catalog. Also called offers catalog, catalog of offers, product catalog. Examples: "An organization has an offer catalog of its products.", "A service has an offer catalog of its packages.", "The person maintains an offer catalog."

candidates.label: hasPOS
candidates.comment: A point-of-sale relation between an organization or person and a place where they operate a point of sale. Also called operates POS, sales location, retail point. Examples: "An organization has a POS in New York.", "The vendor has a POS at the market.", "This company operates multiple POS locations."

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

relations.definition: Indicates belonging to a group or organization.
relations.embedding_query_text: was member of: Indicates belonging to a group or organization.

chosen_property.label: memberOf
chosen_property.justification: The 'memberOf' property directly links a Person to an Organization (PerformingGroup is an Organization) they belong to.

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: musicGroupMember
candidates.comment: A person who is a member of a music group. Also called band member, group member, musician in group. Examples: "The Beatles musicGroupMember 'John Lennon'", "Queen musicGroupMember 'Freddie Mercury'", "Fleetwood Mac musicGroupMember 'Stevie Nicks'". Distinct from member, which is a general property for any organization.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: affiliation
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a person and an organization they are associated with. Also called associated with, member of, works for, belongs to. Examples: "A professor's affiliation is 'Harvard University'.", "A player's affiliation is 'Local Soccer Club'." Distinct from alumniOf, which specifies a past association with an educational organization.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: employee
candidates.comment: An employment relation between an organization and a person who works for it. Also called "works for", "staff member", "on staff". Examples: "Organization 'Google' employee 'Sundar Pichai'", "Company 'Acme Corp' employee 'Jane Doe'", "Restaurant 'The Bistro' employee 'Chef John'". Distinct from member, which indicates a general affiliation rather than an employment relationship.

candidates.label: alumni
candidates.comment: An alumni relation between an educational organization or organization and a person who is a former student or member. Also called former student, graduate, past member. Examples: "A university's alumni include 'Jane Doe'.", "The club's alumni include 'John Smith'." Distinct from alumniOf, which describes the inverse relationship (person to organization).

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

relations.definition: Indicates the time period when someone or something became widely known.
relations.embedding_query_text: became household name in: Indicates the time period when someone or something became widely known.

chosen_property.label: becameWidelyKnownIn
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the time period during which an entity became widely recognized or famous.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly captures the concept of an entity becoming widely known in a specific time period.

candidates.label: familyName
candidates.comment: A family name relation between a person and their last name. Also called: last name, surname. Examples: "John Doe" family name "Doe", "Jane Smith" family name "Smith", "Alice Wonderland" family name "Wonderland". Distinct from givenName, which is the first name.

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: givenName
candidates.comment: A given name relation between a person and their first name. Also called: first name, personal name. Examples: "John Doe" given name "John", "Jane Smith" given name "Jane", "Alice Wonderland" given name "Alice". Distinct from familyName, which is the last name.

candidates.label: name
candidates.comment: A name or title identifying a thing. Also called title, designation, appellation, label. Examples: "Book name 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy'", "Person name 'Alice Smith'", "Company name 'Acme Corp'". Distinct from alternateName, which is an alias or alternative name.

candidates.label: birthDate
candidates.comment: A date representing a person's birth. Also called: date of birth, birthday. Examples: "Person 'John Doe' birthDate '1980-05-15'", "Person 'Jane Smith' birthDate '1992-11-22'."

candidates.label: temporalCoverage
candidates.comment: A temporal scope relation between a creative work and the specific time period that its content describes or applies to. Also called "time period covered", "content timeframe", "temporal scope", "date range of content". Examples: "A census dataset has temporalCoverage 2011/2012", "The historical novel's temporalCoverage is 1939/1945", "This research paper's temporalCoverage is 2015-11/..". Distinct from temporal, which is a more general temporal association when the specific scope is not known.

candidates.label: cookTime
candidates.comment: A temporal measurement for a recipe, indicating the duration required to cook the dish. Also called "cooking duration", "preparation time", "time to cook". Examples: "Recipe 'Chicken Curry' cookTime 'PT30M'", "Recipe 'Cake' cookTime 'PT45M'". Distinct from prepTime, which is the time for preparation before cooking, and totalTime, which is the sum of all time.

candidates.label: ownedFrom
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was obtained. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, date acquired. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2020-01-15'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2018-06-01T10:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2023-03-10'". Distinct from ownedThrough, which is the date ownership ended.

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: characterName
candidates.comment: A naming relation for a performance role, indicating the name of the character being played. Also called "role name", "played character", "fictional name". Examples: "Actor's performance role characterName 'Hamlet'", "Actress's performance role characterName 'Juliet'". Distinct from character, which refers to the fictional person itself, whereas characterName is the name of the character in a specific performance.

chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly links a Person to a TVSeries as its original host.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: firstPerformance
candidates.comment: A first performance relation between a music composition and the event where it was initially performed. Also called: premiere, debut performance, initial staging. Examples: "Beethoven's 5th Symphony" first performance "Vienna, 1808 Concert", "Hamilton Musical" first performance "Public Theater, NYC 2015", "New Opera 'The Siren'" first performance "Royal Opera House Gala".

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly links an AwardReceptionEvent to the Specialty for which the award was given.

candidates.label: award
candidates.comment: An award won by or for a creative work, organization, person, product, or service. Also called: honor, prize, recognition. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' award 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' award 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' award 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from awards, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: awards
candidates.comment: Awards won by or for a creative work, organization, person, or product. Also called: honors, prizes, recognitions. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' awards 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' awards 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' awards 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from award, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: educationalCredentialAwarded
candidates.comment: An educational credential awarded relation between a course or program and the credential received upon successful completion. Also called "award received", "qualification granted", "certificate earned". Examples: "Course 'Introduction to Python' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Certificate of Completion'", "Program 'MBA' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Master of Business Administration'", "Training 'First Aid' educationalCredentialAwarded 'First Aid Certification'".

candidates.label: serviceAudience
candidates.comment: The specific group of people or entities for whom a service is intended or eligible. Also called target audience, service recipients, eligible users. Examples: `Healthcare Service` serviceAudience `Audience: Seniors`, `Educational Service` serviceAudience `Audience: Students`, `Financial Service` serviceAudience `Audience: Small Businesses`.

candidates.label: areaServed
candidates.comment: An area served relation between a contact point, offer, organization, or service and the geographic region where it is available. Also called service area, coverage region, delivery zone. Examples: "A restaurant's area served is 'Downtown'.", "The delivery service's area served is 'California'.", "An organization's area served is 'Worldwide'."

candidates.label: serviceArea
candidates.comment: The geographical region or area where a service is available or provided. Also called service region, coverage area, operational zone. Examples: `Delivery Service` serviceArea `GeoShape: New York City`, `Local Business` serviceArea `AdministrativeArea: California`, `Customer Support` serviceArea `Place: United States`. Distinct from `areaServed`, which is a more general property for things like organizations.

candidates.label: eligibleRegion
candidates.comment: An eligible region relation between an action access specification, delivery charge specification, demand, or offer and the geo-political region(s) for which it is valid. Also called "valid region", "service area", "delivery zone". Examples: "Offer 'Free Shipping' eligibleRegion 'US'", "Delivery charge eligibleRegion 'Europe'", "Demand 'Local Services' eligibleRegion 'New York City'". Distinct from ineligibleRegion, which specifies regions where the offer is not valid.

candidates.label: candidate
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a vote action, indicating the person who is being voted for. Also called "voted for", "nominee", "electoral candidate". Examples: "Election vote action candidate Jane Smith", "Award vote action candidate John Doe".

candidates.label: area
candidates.comment: An area relation between a broadcast service and the geographic place where its users can access it. Also called service region, coverage area, broadcast zone. Examples: "A radio station's area is 'Greater London'.", "The TV service's area is 'North America'."

chosen_property.label: pertainsToSeriesCount
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the number or specific range of series to which a co-presentation event relates.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly links an Event to a SeriesNumber indicating the count of series it pertains to.

candidates.label: numberOfSeasons
candidates.comment: The total number of seasons within a radio series, TV series, or video game series. Also called season count, series seasons, total seasons. Examples: "TV Series X numberOfSeasons 10", "Radio Series Y numberOfSeasons 3", "Video Game Series Z numberOfSeasons 5". Distinct from numberOfEpisodes, which is for individual episodes within a season or series.

candidates.label: numberOfEpisodes
candidates.comment: The total number of episodes within a creative work season, radio series, TV series, or video game series. Also called episode count, series episodes, season episodes. Examples: "TV Series X numberOfEpisodes 200", "Season 1 numberOfEpisodes 10", "Video Game Series Y numberOfEpisodes 5". Distinct from numTracks, which is for music.

candidates.label: seasons
candidates.comment: A collection of seasons that constitute a radio, TV, or video game series. Also called series seasons, show seasons, installments. Examples: `TV Series: Game of Thrones` seasons `[Season 1, Season 2, ...]`, `Video Game Series: Call of Duty` seasons `[Modern Warfare Season, Cold War Season]`, `Radio Drama` seasons `[Season A, Season B]`. Distinct from `season`, which typically refers to a single season.

candidates.label: seasonNumber
candidates.comment: The numerical or textual identifier indicating a season's position within an ordered series of seasons. Also called season index, season position, season number in series. Examples: `TV Show Season` seasonNumber `1`, `Anime Series Season` seasonNumber `"Part 2"`, `Video Game Season Pass` seasonNumber `3`.

candidates.label: season
candidates.comment: A specific season within a radio, TV, or video game series. Also called series season, season of show, installment season. Examples: `TV Series: The Crown` season `CreativeWorkSeason: Season 4`, `Video Game Series: FIFA` season `URL to FIFA 23 Season`, `Radio Series: The Archers` season `CreativeWorkSeason: 2022 Season`. Distinct from `seasons`, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: numTracks
candidates.comment: The total number of tracks contained within a music playlist or album. Also called track count, song count, number of songs. Examples: "Album X numTracks 12", "Playlist Y numTracks 50", "EP Z numTracks 4". Distinct from numberOfEpisodes, which is for seasons or series.

candidates.label: containsSeason
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a radio, TV, or video game series and a creative work season that is part of it. Also called "includes season", "has season", "season of series". Examples: "TV series 'Friends' containsSeason 'Season 1'", "Video game series 'Halo' containsSeason 'Halo: Combat Evolved'".

candidates.label: episodes
candidates.comment: An episodes relation between a creative work season, radio series, TV series, or video game series and the episodes it contains. Also called "contains episodes", "features episodes", "series parts". Examples: "TV series 'Friends' episodes 'All 10 seasons'", "Creative work season 'Season 1' episodes 'All 22 episodes'", "Video game series 'Halo' episodes 'All main titles'". Distinct from episode, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: numberOfLoanPayments
candidates.comment: The total number of payments contractually required to repay a loan. Also called loan payment count, repayment installments, number of installments. Examples: "Mortgage Repayment numberOfLoanPayments 360", "Car Loan Repayment numberOfLoanPayments 60", "Personal Loan Repayment numberOfLoanPayments 24".

candidates.label: issueNumber
candidates.comment: A publication identifier relation between a publication issue and its specific identifying number or designation within a series. Also called issue ID, volume number, edition number, publication identifier. Examples: A journal issue has an issueNumber of '5'. A comic book has an issueNumber of 'Vol. 2, Issue #3'. A magazine has an issueNumber of 'Summer 2023'. Distinct from volumeNumber, which is for the larger volume a publication issue belongs to.

relations.definition: Indicates the year or period when something began.
relations.embedding_query_text: started in: Indicates the year or period when something began.

chosen_property.label: startDate
chosen_property.justification: The 'startDate' property indicates the beginning date of an Event, which aligns with 'started in' for events occurring in a specific year (Duration interpreted as Date).

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.

candidates.label: startOffset
candidates.comment: A temporal offset indicating the start time of a clip or action, measured in seconds from the beginning of a larger work. Also called "clip start time", "beginning offset", "time offset start", "seek start". Examples: "The video clip has startOffset 30 seconds", "The action's startOffset is 120 seconds into the recording", "This segment begins at startOffset 0."

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: copyrightYear
candidates.comment: A temporal relation between a creative work and the year its copyright was first asserted. Also called: year of copyright, copyright date, first copyright year. Examples: "Classic Album" copyright year "1970", "Software Version 1.0" copyright year "2005", "Research Paper" copyright year "2022". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first publication or broadcast.

candidates.label: jobStartDate
candidates.comment: An employment start date relation between a job posting and the anticipated date for a successful applicant to begin work. Also called start date, commencement date, employment beginning. Examples: A job posting has a jobStartDate of '2024-09-01'. A job posting has a jobStartDate of 'Fall 2024'. A job posting has a jobStartDate of 'as soon as possible'. Distinct from jobImmediateStart, which is a boolean flag for immediate availability.

candidates.label: yearBuilt
candidates.comment: A construction year relation between an accommodation and a number, indicating the year in which the accommodation was built. Also called construction year, built year, year of construction. Examples: Hotel yearBuilt 1985, ApartmentBuilding yearBuilt 2010, House yearBuilt 1950.

candidates.label: dateCreated
candidates.comment: A temporal origin relation between a creative work or data feed item and the date it was created or added. Also called: creation date, date of origin, initial date. Examples: "Painting" date created "1889-05-01", "Blog Post" date created "2023-03-15T10:00:00Z", "Data Feed Entry" date created "2023-01-01". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first public release.

candidates.label: availabilityStarts
candidates.comment: A date or time marking the beginning of availability for a product or service in an offer or access specification. Also called: availability start date, offer start, access start time. Examples: "Offer 'New Product' availabilityStarts '2023-11-01'", "ActionAccessSpecification 'Pre-sale' availabilityStarts '2023-10-20T09:00:00'". Distinct from availabilityEnds, which marks the end.

candidates.label: foundingDate
candidates.comment: A founding date relation between an organization and the specific date it was established. Also called: establishment date, creation date, inception date. Examples: "Microsoft" founding date "1975-04-04", "Apple Inc." founding date "1976-04-01", "Google" founding date "1998-09-04".

relations.definition: Indicates the program from which a person was removed or departed.
relations.embedding_query_text: from program: Indicates the program from which a person was removed or departed.

chosen_property.label: departedFromProgram
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the television series from which a person departed during a program departure event.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly links a ProgramDepartureEvent to the TVSeries from which a person departed.

candidates.label: dateDeleted
candidates.comment: A temporal removal relation between a data feed item and the datetime it was removed from the feed. Also called: deletion date, removal date, date of removal. Examples: "Expired Job Posting" date deleted "2023-06-30", "Outdated Product Listing" date deleted "2023-01-01T00:00:00Z".

candidates.label: programName
candidates.comment: A program name relation between a program membership and the textual name of the program it represents. Also called name of program, membership program name. Examples: "A frequent flyer membership has a program name 'SkyMiles'.", "A hotel loyalty membership has a program name 'Hilton Honors'.", "A gym membership has a program name 'Gold's Gym Basic'.". Distinct from program, which links to a structured MemberProgram entity.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: program
candidates.comment: An association between a program membership and the specific member program it belongs to. Also called part of program, associated program, membership program. Examples: "A loyalty card membership is part of the 'Star Alliance Gold' program.", "A gym membership is part of the 'Premium Fitness' program.", "A frequent flyer membership is part of the 'SkyMiles' program.". Distinct from programName, which is the textual name of the program.

candidates.label: departurePlatform
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a train trip and the platform from which it departs. Also called: platform number, train platform, departure track. Examples: "Train to Paris" departure platform "Platform 5", "Commuter Train" departure platform "Track 3". Distinct from arrivalPlatform, which is the arrival platform.

candidates.label: applicationDeadline
candidates.comment: An application deadline relation between an educational or occupational program and the date or text indicating when applications close for an enrollment cycle. Also called submission deadline, application closing date, enrollment cutoff. Examples: "A university program's application deadline is '2023-03-15'.", "The training program's application deadline is 'Rolling admissions'."

candidates.label: programMembershipUsed
candidates.comment: A program membership application relation between a reservation and the loyalty program membership used for it. Also called applied membership, loyalty program for, membership applied to. Examples: "A flight reservation used a 'MileagePlus Gold' program membership.", "A hotel reservation used a 'Marriott Bonvoy Platinum' program membership.", "A car rental reservation used an 'Emerald Club' program membership."

candidates.label: termDuration
candidates.comment: A duration representing the length of a term of study within an educational or occupational program. Also called "term length", "semester duration", "quarter length", "study period duration". Examples: "The program has termDuration 15 weeks", "The educational program's termDuration is 10 weeks", "This course has a termDuration of one semester."

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

relations.definition: Specifies the length of time an event or condition lasted.
relations.embedding_query_text: duration: Specifies the length of time an event or condition lasted.

chosen_property.label: duration
chosen_property.justification: The 'duration' property directly links an Event (MentalHealthStruggleEvent) to its length of time.

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: timeToComplete
candidates.comment: A duration representing the expected length of time to complete an educational or occupational program when attending full-time. Also called "program duration", "completion duration", "full-time study length", "expected completion time". Examples: "The degree program has timeToComplete 4 years", "The certification's timeToComplete is 6 months", "This program requires timeToComplete 2 years of full-time study."

candidates.label: billingDuration
candidates.comment: A duration, number, or quantitative value specifying how long a price or price component will be billed. Also called: billing period length, contractual duration, payment plan length. Examples: "UnitPriceSpecification 'Subscription' billingDuration 'P1Y' (1 year)", "UnitPriceSpecification 'Service Plan' billingDuration '12' (months)."

candidates.label: durationOfWarranty
candidates.comment: A warranty duration relation between a warranty promise and the quantitative value representing its length. Also called "warranty period", "guarantee length", "coverage duration". Examples: "Laptop warranty durationOfWarranty 'P1Y'", "Car warranty durationOfWarranty 'P3Y'", "Appliance warranty durationOfWarranty 'P6M'". Distinct from duration, which is a general property for the length of various items.

candidates.label: activityDuration
candidates.comment: An activity duration relation between an exercise plan and the length of time recommended for engaging in the activity. Also called exercise length, workout time, session duration. Examples: "An exercise plan's activity duration is '30 minutes'.", "The yoga routine's activity duration is '1 hour'."

candidates.label: termDuration
candidates.comment: A duration representing the length of a term of study within an educational or occupational program. Also called "term length", "semester duration", "quarter length", "study period duration". Examples: "The program has termDuration 15 weeks", "The educational program's termDuration is 10 weeks", "This course has a termDuration of one semester."

candidates.label: observationPeriod
candidates.comment: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.

candidates.label: eligibleDuration
candidates.comment: An eligible duration relation between a demand or offer and the quantitative value representing the period for which it is valid. Also called "validity period", "offer duration", "term length". Examples: "Offer 'Limited Time Sale' eligibleDuration 'P7D'", "Subscription offer eligibleDuration 'P1Y'", "Demand 'Project Bid' eligibleDuration 'P30D'".

candidates.label: leaseLength
candidates.comment: A rental term relation between an accommodation, offer, or real estate listing and the duration of its lease agreement. Also called lease duration, rental period, term of lease, tenancy length. Examples: An accommodation has a leaseLength of '12 months'. An offer specifies a leaseLength of '2 years'. A real estate listing has a leaseLength of '6-month minimum'. Distinct from duration, which is a general duration for any event or item.

candidates.label: timeRequired
candidates.comment: A duration representing the approximate time typically needed for an audience to engage with or complete a creative work. Also called "completion time", "estimated duration", "reading time", "viewing time". Examples: "The article has timeRequired 10 minutes", "The course's timeRequired is 40 hours", "This creative work takes timeRequired 2 hours to watch."

relations.definition: Indicates a specific health or mental state as part of a broader struggle.
relations.embedding_query_text: includes condition: Indicates a specific health or mental state as part of a broader struggle.

instances: Oddie struggles with mental health -> depression
Oddie struggles with mental health -> bipolar disorder

chosen_property.label: includesMedicalCondition
chosen_property.definition: Indicates a specific medical condition that is part of a broader mental health struggle event.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly links a MentalHealthStruggleEvent to a MedicalCondition it includes.

candidates.label: healthCondition
candidates.comment: A health condition relation between a medical study, patient, or people audience and an associated medical condition. Also called medical diagnosis, health status, condition of. Examples: "A patient has a health condition of diabetes.", "A medical study focuses on a health condition.", "The target audience has a health condition of hypertension."

candidates.label: status
candidates.comment: An indication of the current state or status of a medical condition, procedure, or study. Also called "current state", "condition status", "study progress", "procedure status". Examples: "The medical study has status Recruiting", "The patient's condition status is stable", "The procedure's status is completed."

candidates.label: signOrSymptom
candidates.comment: An objective sign or subjective symptom that is a manifestation of a medical condition. Also called condition indicator, medical manifestation, health sign. Examples: `Flu` signOrSymptom `MedicalSignOrSymptom: Fever`, `Depression` signOrSymptom `MedicalSignOrSymptom: Persistent Sadness`, `Broken Leg` signOrSymptom `MedicalSignOrSymptom: Swelling`. Distinct from `diagnosis`, which is the identification of the condition itself.

candidates.label: relatedCondition
candidates.comment: A related condition relation between an anatomical structure or system and a medical condition associated with it. Also called associated condition, condition of, affects condition. Examples: "The knee joint has a related condition 'arthritis'.", "The respiratory system has a related condition 'asthma'.", "The skin has a related condition 'eczema'."

candidates.label: drug
candidates.comment: A drug relation between a medical entity (such as a drug class, condition, patient, or therapeutic procedure) and a specific drug or medicine. Also called "medication used", "prescribed drug", "contains drug". Examples: "Medical condition 'Hypertension' drug 'Lisinopril'", "Therapeutic procedure 'Chemotherapy' drug 'Paclitaxel'", "Drug class 'Statins' drug 'Atorvastatin'".

candidates.label: significance
candidates.comment: The medical or diagnostic importance of superficial anatomy, indicating how its characteristics may suggest underlying conditions or treatments. Also called clinical relevance, diagnostic implication, anatomical importance. Examples: `Skin Lesion` significance `"May indicate melanoma"`, `Swollen Lymph Node` significance `"Could suggest infection"`, `Discolored Nail Bed` significance `"Possible circulatory issue"`.

candidates.label: includedRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A risk factor inclusion relation between a medical risk estimator and a risk factor used in its calculation. Also called risk factor in calculation, factor considered, included element. Examples: "A medical risk estimator includes a risk factor of age.", "The estimator considers an included risk factor of smoking.", "This tool uses an included risk factor for calculation."

candidates.label: riskFactor
candidates.comment: A factor that increases the likelihood of a patient developing a specific medical condition. Also called predisposing factor, risk element, vulnerability factor. Examples: `Heart Disease` riskFactor `High Cholesterol`, `Diabetes` riskFactor `Obesity`, `Lung Cancer` riskFactor `Smoking`.

candidates.label: itemCondition
candidates.comment: A product state relation indicating the physical condition of a product or service, or the condition required for returns. Also called product state, condition of item, quality status, return condition. Examples: An offer has an itemCondition of 'NewCondition'. A product has an itemCondition of 'UsedCondition'. A return policy specifies itemCondition 'SellerRefurbished'.

candidates.label: possibleTreatment
candidates.comment: A medical attribute indicating a potential treatment, drug, or therapy to address a medical condition, sign, or symptom. Also called potential therapy, recommended treatment, intervention option. Examples: A medical condition has a possible treatment of 'antibiotics'. A symptom has a possible treatment of 'pain relievers'. Hypertension has a possible treatment of 'lifestyle modification'.

relations.definition: Indicates a causal relationship where one event resulted in another.
relations.embedding_query_text: led to: Indicates a causal relationship where one event resulted in another.

instances: Oddie dropped from Springwatch -> Oddie struggles with mental health

chosen_property.label: resultedInEvent
chosen_property.definition: Indicates an event that was caused by or resulted from another event.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly links one Event (cause) to another Event (effect) with a causal meaning.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: data
candidates.comment: An association relation between an instantaneous event and the data linked to it. Also called: event data, associated data, event information. Examples: "Sensor Reading Event" data "temperature: 25C, humidity: 60%", "Log Entry Event" data "User 'admin' logged in from IP 192.168.1.1", "System Alert Event" data "Error code 500: Database connection failed".

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: lifeEvent
candidates.comment: A life event relation between a person and a significant event in their life. Also called: significant event, personal milestone, biographical event. Examples: "John Doe lifeEvent Baptism", "Jane Smith lifeEvent Graduation Ceremony", "Family lifeEvent Wedding".

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

relations.definition: Indicates a leadership role within an organization.
relations.embedding_query_text: was vice president of: Indicates a leadership role within an organization.

chosen_property.label: worksFor
chosen_property.justification: The 'worksFor' property indicates an employment or formal role of a Person within an Organization (NGO is an Organization).

candidates.label: jobTitle
candidates.comment: An occupational role relation between a person and their formal designation within an organization. Also called position, role, occupation, professional title. Examples: A person has a jobTitle of 'Software Engineer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Chief Executive Officer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Marketing Manager'.

candidates.label: namedPosition
candidates.comment: A specific named position or role played by a person or organization within a larger organization. Also called role name, position title, job title. Examples: "Athlete Role namedPosition 'Quarterback'", "Employee Role namedPosition 'Senior Software Engineer'", "Board Member Role namedPosition 'Treasurer'". Distinct from roleName, which is a more general description of a role.

candidates.label: numberedPosition
candidates.comment: A number associated with an organization role, such as an athlete's jersey number. Also called role number, position number, identifier number. candidates.comment: A content suitability relation indicating whether a creative work, offer, or product is appropriate for families. Also called family-safe, suitable for all ages, kid-friendly, appropriate for families. Examples: A movie has isFamilyFriendly set to 'true'. A video game has isFamilyFriendly set to 'false'. A restaurant offer has isFamilyFriendly set to 'true'.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: sibling
candidates.comment: A familial relationship between two people who share at least one parent. Also called brother, sister, kin, family member. Examples: `John Doe` sibling `Jane Doe`, `Mary Smith` sibling `Tom Smith`, `Alice Brown` sibling `Bob Brown`. Distinct from `siblings`, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

chosen_property.label: hasOccupation
chosen_property.justification: The 'hasOccupation' property directly links a Person to their Occupation.

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: author
candidates.comment: An organization or person who created content or a rating. Also called: creator, writer, originator, composer. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Novel' author 'Jane Austen'", "Rating 'Product Review' author 'Consumer Reports'", "CreativeWork 'Article' author 'New York Times'". Distinct from artist, which is typically for visual or comic art.

candidates.label: alumni
candidates.comment: An alumni relation between an educational organization or organization and a person who is a former student or member. Also called former student, graduate, past member. Examples: "A university's alumni include 'Jane Doe'.", "The club's alumni include 'John Smith'." Distinct from alumniOf, which describes the inverse relationship (person to organization).

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: parent
candidates.comment: A person who is a parent of another person. Also called mother, father, progenitor. Examples: "Child A parent 'Parent B'", "Person X parent 'Mother Y'", "Person Z parent 'Father W'". Distinct from children, which describes the offspring.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: name
candidates.comment: A name or title identifying a thing. Also called title, designation, appellation, label. Examples: "Book name 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy'", "Person name 'Alice Smith'", "Company name 'Acme Corp'". Distinct from alternateName, which is an alias or alternative name.

chosen_property.label: guestOfHonourFor
chosen_property.definition: Indicates a sports team for which a person was a guest of honour.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly links a Person to a SportsTeam as a guest of honour.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: additionalNumberOfGuests
candidates.comment: An additional number of guests relation between an RSVP action and the count of extra attendees beyond the invitee. Also called plus-one count, extra guests, total additional attendees. Examples: "An RSVP action's additional number of guests is '2'.", "The wedding RSVP indicates an additional number of guests of '1'."

candidates.label: award
candidates.comment: An award won by or for a creative work, organization, person, product, or service. Also called: honor, prize, recognition. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' award 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' award 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' award 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from awards, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: honorificPrefix
candidates.comment: An honorific prefix relation between a person and a title preceding their name. Also called title, salutation, courtesy title. Examples: "A person has an honorific prefix 'Dr.'.", "Her honorific prefix is 'Ms.'.", "The individual uses the honorific prefix 'Mr.'."

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: lifeEvent
candidates.comment: A life event relation between a person and a significant event in their life. Also called: significant event, personal milestone, biographical event. Examples: "John Doe lifeEvent Baptism", "Jane Smith lifeEvent Graduation Ceremony", "Family lifeEvent Wedding".

candidates.label: numAdults
candidates.comment: The number of adults included in a lodging reservation. Also called adult count, number of grown-ups, adult guests. Examples: "Hotel Reservation numAdults 2", "Vacation Rental numAdults 4", "Single Room Reservation numAdults 1". Distinct from numChildren, which specifies the number of children.

candidates.label: alumni
candidates.comment: An alumni relation between an educational organization or organization and a person who is a former student or member. Also called former student, graduate, past member. Examples: "A university's alumni include 'Jane Doe'.", "The club's alumni include 'John Smith'." Distinct from alumniOf, which describes the inverse relationship (person to organization).

candidates.label: honorificSuffix
candidates.comment: An honorific suffix relation between a person and a title following their name. Also called post-nominal title, suffix title, academic suffix. Examples: "A person has an honorific suffix 'PhD'.", "His honorific suffix is 'M.D.'.", "The individual uses the honorific suffix 'Jr.'."
